requirement:
When preparing the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, every terminology definition
referenced by the subject or any contributed source MUST contribute its complete
fenced declaration, including its phrase option. Definitions referenced by those
definitions MUST also be included transitively, without duplicates or
nontermination on cycles.

When an additional source read introduces a terminology dependency, the same
complete, transitive definition set MUST be supplied to the model and recorded
before accepting a submission.
rationale:
**Judgment: the requirement is met.** The implementation covers each obligation and is marked `{impl}`. Tests cover the main cases and some failure paths.

**Initial mandatory set** (`AssessmentSources::prepare`, `src/authoring/inputs.rs`):
- `prepare` collects the subject declaration, cited requirements, and `{impl}`/`{test}`/anchor sources into `mandatory`.
- It then calls `definition_inputs(..., &mandatory, Some(&subject.text))`.
- That function calls `terms::dependencies` (`src/terms.rs`). `direct_references` takes terms from the subject text and from every contributed input:
  - Rust sources are scanned in comments only.
  - Markdown sources are scanned as Markdown.
  - Requirements declarations are scanned by body.
  - Definition inputs contribute themselves.
- `close_dependencies` expands to a fixed point using a `visited` set and a `BTreeSet`, so there are no duplicates and cycles terminate.
- An unresolvable term or a malformed declaration returns an error (`.map_err(io::Error::other)`).
- Each term becomes `InputSelector::Definition`, resolved through `source_input`. `resolve` uses `target.raw_lines`, which is the complete fenced declaration including the `:phrase:` line.
- Already-present inputs are not added twice (`!mandatory.contains`).
- Built-ins have no term references, so they add no dependencies.

**Additional reads** (`additional_definitions`, `record_inputs`, `converse`, `tools::read`, `tools::search`):
- Every habeas read (outline, line-range, requirements, or definition selector) and every ripgrep search calls `additional_definitions`. It computes the transitive closure over the newly read inputs and drops definitions already in those inputs or in `recorded`.
- The definitions are returned in the tool result, so the model sees them. They are also added to `ToolDelivery.inputs`, which `converse` accumulates in `pending`.
- `converse` calls `sources.record_inputs(&pending)` right after each provider response and before it handles a submission or accepts a result. This gives "supplied and recorded before accepting a submission". `record_inputs` also deduplicates.
- One minor point: when two tool calls in the same turn need the same new term, it is delivered twice to the model. It is still recorded once, which is what the requirement's "without duplicates" refers to.

**Marking:** All code that implements the requirement carries `{impl}`: `prepare`, `record_inputs`, `additional_definitions`, `source_input`, `definition_inputs`, `converse`, `tools::read`, and `tools::search`. The shared closure logic in `src/terms.rs` is marked for `requirements.definitions.dependencies`, and that requirement's text carries out its part of this one. I found no behavior beyond what the requirement specifies.

**Tests:**
- `bundle_combines_direct_references_terms_and_current_existing_selectors` (`inputs.rs`) uses a cyclic pair of terms where the requirement references only `terms.unit` directly. It asserts exactly two definition inputs, so `terms.value` comes in transitively and without duplicates. It also asserts that an unrelated requirement is excluded.
- `mandatory_git_inputs_require_staging_declarations_sources_and_terms` checks a term referenced from a Rust `{impl}` comment, and that an unstaged term file is reported.
- `definitions_introduced_by_a_read_are_supplied_and_recorded_before_submission` (`mod.rs`) is an end-to-end test of the second paragraph:
  - A read introduces a cyclic pair of terms.
  - The result contains the transitive set, each term once, and each as a complete `:::{definition}` plus `:phrase:` declaration.
  - The second request, which carries the submission, contains the definition text; the first request does not.
  - The evidence record contains those definitions.
- `reading_records_only_delivered_sources_and_their_terms` and `search_supplies_terminology_clamps_at_eof_and_reports_failures` cover the `habeas` and `ripgrep` tools, including the recorded definitions.

One gap: the authoring tests contain no direct case for a missing term during `prepare`. That error path (`term X: no matching named definition`) is covered by tests in `src/evidence.rs`, notably `configuration_and_dependency_failures_do_not_stop_later_checks`. I do not consider this material.

text: :::{req} authoring_inputs
When preparing the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, every terminology definition
referenced by the subject or any contributed source MUST contribute its complete
fenced declaration, including its phrase option. Definitions referenced by those
definitions MUST also be included transitively, without duplicates or
nontermination on cycles.
When an additional source read introduces a terminology dependency, the same
complete, transitive definition set MUST be supplied to the model and recorded
before accepting a submission.
:::{req} mandatory_inputs
The harness MUST construct each assessment's mandatory input set by combining
the contributions specified by the requirements applicable to that subject and
its inputs. A requirement that contributes inputs MUST cite this requirement and
define which sources it contributes and when. The harness MUST include every
applicable contribution, deduplicate identical selections, and report
unresolvable mandatory inputs before inference. The complete set MUST be supplied
in the initial model request.
Generated output under project-root `evidence/`, including symlink aliases, MUST
be omitted from mandatory inputs when the default exclusion applies. An explicit
workspace allow MUST permit those selections; an explicit disallow MUST abort
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial`.
:::{req} dependencies
Requirement and example evidence MUST include a definition input for every term referenced by its subject text or reviewed inputs.

Habeas MUST repeatedly include definitions referenced by required definitions until the set reaches a fixed point. Each required definition MUST have exactly one definition input per evidence record. Cyclic references MUST be permitted and MUST NOT cause repeated expansion or nontermination.
Validation MUST report missing required definition inputs and MUST NOT silently refresh snapshots.
